newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-BATTLING WOOSNAM CLINGS TO THE LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BATTLING WOOSNAM CLINGS TO THE LEAD.

text.p: Ian Woosnam battled bumpy greens to cling to a one-shot lead with a two-under-par 70 in the third round of the British PGA Championship at Wentworth on Sunday.
The Welsh Ryder Cup player led on 11-under-par 205 from Irishman Darren Clarke, who matched his opening round 66 to hold second place.
South African Ernie Els with a 67 containing two eagles on the back nine and Nick Faldo with a 70 shared third spot another shot back on 207.
Stephen Ames of Trinidad would have joined them but for a two-shot penalty the 12th green.
His ball moved on address, but he did not realise it and did not replace it. Referee John Paramor reviewed the incident with Ames on a video tape after the round and Ames agreed the ball had moved.
That was a penalty of one stroke and he incurred the second for not replacing the ball to its original ppsition.
His subsquent 70 left him in joint fifth on seven under with English Ryder Cup player David Gilford, who carded a 72.
European number one Colin Montgomerie soared to a 76 to fall out of contention after blocking several tee shots into trouble on the right.
Woosnam played superbly from tee to green apart from a couple of bad drives, but a double bogey six at the ninth was unlucky.
His drive found the rough and he got a flier with a seven-iron that sailed over the green into a difficult lie.
From there he chipped 25 feet past the pin and three-putted.
They were his only dropped shots in a steady and at times spectacular round.

At the 452-yard third he struck a seven-iron second straight over a greenside bunker onto the three-tiered green. The ball took a big bounce and finished on the top level with the pin on the second tier, yet he rolled his putt unerringly down the slope 25 feet into the hole for a birdie.
Later, however, he missed from five feet for birdie at the 16th and from 10 feet at the last.
"The greens are not very good at all. The ball was bouncing everywhere," he said. "You look at a putt and the putt takes a turn. They jump all over the place.
"The course is in great shape except for the greens. Maybe it's the weather we have had. It just seems strange," he said.
Clarke, the burly Northern Ireland player who shared the first round lead, carded his third 66 in four days including Thursday's pro-am but could not account for his second-round 74.
"But I'm right back in there," said Clarke, who looks certain to make his Ryder Cup debut for Europe against the Americans this year.
He birdied the first four holes and had three more birdies and an eagle but dropped shots at three short holes.
"I hit poor shots into those greens. I must do some work with my mid-irons," he said.
Faldo, here to chase much needed Ryder Cup points, also found the greens bumpy and uneven and said he had trouble getting the ball to the hole.
He, like Woosnam, played superbly from tee to green and his only blip came at the 17th where he three-putted from 15 feet, missing a second putt of just two feet.
At the long last hole he drove into a bunker, hit the lip getting out and took four to reach the green, but holed from 45 feet to save his par.
Els's 67 contained three successive birdies from the second and eagle threes at the 12th from 50 feet and the 18th from 25 feet.
But he also had two bogeys on the back nine, including one at the 15th where he missed a two-foot putt.
At the 571-yard 17th his drive strayed into deep rough and he needed four shots to reach the green, where he two putted from 18 feet.
"I let it slip at the 15th when I had everything under control. Now I think I'll have to shoot the same score tomorrow to have a chance," he said.
Montgomerie, Europe's number one for four years, had little to say after slipping seven shots away from his two opening 69s to joint 18th place nine shots off the lead.
"I didn't play very well but I tried on every shot and that was the best I could do.
"Yes, I was blocking my shots. It doesn't take an Einstein to figure that out," he said.
